subject: Pilot ingest handshake — burst SLA hypotheses and owners
messages_raw:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Gupta <maya@aurora.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ingest handshake — burst SLA hypotheses and owners

Hi Maya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align teams for the pilot (RDW-2387):

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: customer-facing completion API that powers search & summarization in Aurora’s app.
- Expected steady-state RPS: ~20 rps during business hours.
- Burst windows: 3x sustained bursts up to ~60 rps for 10–20 minutes; rare spikes up to ~120 rps (~1–2x / week).
- Median token length: 120 tokens; 95th: ~450 tokens (long context + doc snippets).
- Concurrency target: 40 concurrent inferences (client-side concurrency).

Success criteria (proposed)
- 95th percentile latency (inference only): <220ms for median token lengths; <600ms for 95th token lengths during steady-state.
- Error rate: <0.5% request failure rate during burst windows.
- Cost benchmark: target per-1k-token cost within X% of baseline (we’ll quantify after initial probes).
- Stability: KV-cache hit rate improvements for repeat prefixes where applicable.

Pilot plan & timeline
- Week 0: Metadata/traffic snapshot ingestion + confirm telemetry hooks (you provide sample traffic CSV).
- Week 1: Probe runs (low-risk) to validate model variant and tokenization profile.
- Week 2: Controlled burst simulation and latency stress window.
- Week 3: Readout, regressions check, and signoff for canary.

Owners (initial)
- Redwood: Karthik (trial lead), Soojin (ops/runbook), Priyom (benchmarks + probes).
- Aurora: Maya (product/PM), SRE (ingest/telemetry).

Immediate asks for Aurora
1) Share a 24–72 hour sample of production-ish traffic (CSV preferred) with columns: timestamp, request_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, model_hint, status_code.
2) Confirm the busiest local time windows (preferred timezone) and any planned marketing events through the pilot.

Attachments: sample CSV template attached for reference (aurora_traffic_snapshot.csv).

Next steps
- Maya, if you can drop the snapshot and confirm a Friday 10/23 09:00–10:00 PT slot for controlled probe window, we’ll schedule Redwood engineers and provide a short runbook.

Thanks — happy to iterate on the success criteria.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Maya Gupta <maya@aurora.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora SRE <sre@aurora.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ingest handshake — burst SLA hypotheses and owners

Thanks Karthik and team — captured and looks good. I attached a 48h traffic snapshot (aurora_traffic_snapshot.csv) and a short note on our peak windows. Quick clarifications from our side:
- The 120 rps spike is expected during feature rollouts and internal load tests (we can flag test periods).
- Model_hint: clients set a user-level hint; most calls use base-llama-7b. We’re open to trying a smaller/quantized variant for cost tests.
- Telemetry: we can add the additional fields you requested; our SRE will join the probe slot on Friday.

Attachment: aurora_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV, 28 KB)

Maya Gupta
Product Lead, Aurora.ai
maya@aurora.ai

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Gupta <maya@aurora.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 16:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ingest handshake — burst SLA hypotheses and owners

Internal follow-up: I ingested the snapshot into the staging probe harness and ran a quick token-distribution analysis. Highlights:
- Median tokens: 118 (close to their 120 estimate).
- Top 5% includes many long-doc prompts ~400–500 tokens; these are the primary latency pressure points.
- Burst shape: brief ramp to 3x steady-state over ~3 minutes, plateau ~12 minutes, then taper.

Proposed probe plan for Friday 10/23 09:00–10:00 PT (controlled):
- 09:00–09:10: Warmup at 25% steady-state (5 rps) to populate KV cache.
- 09:10–09:30: Steady-state profile at 20 rps.
- 09:30–09:45: Simulated burst (ramp to 60 rps over 3 min, hold 12 min).
- 09:45–10:00: Spike test: three 60–120s micro-spikes to 120 rps, then cool-down.

Owner assignments:
- Soojin: prepare runbook + guardrails (circuit-breaker thresholds, fallback route).
- Priyom: metric collection and readout deck (p95/p99 latency, error rates, token cost).
- Karthik: coordinate Aurora SRE and schedule infra seats.

I created a short MOP checklist for the probe — attaching here (mop_checklist.pdf).

Karthik

Attachments: mop_checklist.pdf (PDF, 45 KB)

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Maya Gupta <maya@aurora.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ingest handshake — burst SLA hypotheses and owners

All set from ops side. Quick notes and one ask:
- Runbook will include exact thresholds we’ll flip (p95 > 600ms => degrade to quantized variant; error rate > 1% => throttle to steady-state).
- We’ll enable token-level traces for the probe window and share pre/post KV-cache hit rates.
- Ask: can Aurora provide a short-lived API key and a test tenant org for the probe? We prefer not to run against production keys.

Pending
- Aurora: test tenant + API key (short TTL).
- Redwood: final runbook posted to the shared link and calendar invite for 10/23 09:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to the probe.

Soojin Lee
Lead Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
